question: Which Linux companion app direction should OpenClaw sponsor now that Windows Hub has shipped: the C/GTK4 track, the Rust/GTK4 alternative, or a deferred/narrower Linux milestone plan?
rationale: Current main only completes the Windows side; the remaining Linux work is a large app architecture and security boundary choice that automation cannot safely choose from code evidence alone.

options.title: Sponsor one GTK Linux track
options.body: Pick one Linux PR as the canonical implementation path and require focused security, packaging, proof, labeler, docs, and maturity updates before merge.

options.title: Split Linux into narrower milestones
options.body: Keep the umbrella open but close or pause large app PRs until maintainers define a smaller first milestone such as tray/status, notifications, or gateway setup.

options.title: Defer official Linux app
options.body: Document Linux Gateway support as the supported path for now and keep desktop companion work external or experimental until ownership is clearer.

recommendation.title: Sponsor one GTK Linux track
recommendation.body: Pick one Linux PR as the canonical implementation path and require focused security, packaging, proof, labeler, docs, and maturity updates before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He opened the tracker, set the GTK-native direction in the discussion, and recently maintained the platform docs that define current user-facing status.
